desc: Remnant of a supernova that exploded about 10,000 years ago in Cygnus. Its filaments glow in oxygen and hydrogen emission.

name: Gum Nebula
desc: A vast faint emission nebula in Vela and Puppis, possibly the old remnant of a supernova, with the Vela pulsar near its heart.

name: Barnard's Loop
desc: A huge arc of ionised hydrogen around the Orion complex, probably inflated by supernovae in the Orion OB1 association.

name: Hyades
desc: The closest open cluster to the Sun, forming the V-shaped face of Taurus. About 625 million years old.

name: Coalsack Nebula
desc: The most prominent dark nebula in the sky, a cloud of dust next to the Southern Cross that blocks the Milky Way behind it.

name: Horsehead Nebula
desc: A dark nebula in Orion silhouetted against the emission nebula IC 434; a column of dust shaped by radiation from Sigma Orionis.

name: Brocchi's Cluster
desc: A chance alignment of stars in Vulpecula that looks like a coat hanger in binoculars.
